subject: ferrum
title: Three-tier tree-sitter-bash authority policy, fail-closed on every parse path, ships ON at medium
evidence: src/tools/shell_guard.rs:66-105 (deny on parser-unavailable/parse-fail/syntax-error/256KB/20k-node/256-depth), src/config.rs:583 (default Medium), src/tools/mod.rs:223, src/agent/mod.rs:9614 (! shortcut same gate)
one_why: Corpus instance x10 of the concept; ferrum's rung is distinctive: low/medium/high as an authority ladder (mutability, substitution, dynamic-command axes) rather than a single deny-list, with all catastrophic shapes rejected tier-independently.

subject: ferrum
title: Repo/project config is monotone-narrowing only: can tighten safety, intersect allow-lists, narrow roots, disable MCP - never loosen or add servers
evidence: src/config.rs:640-644 (stricter_safety + project_safety_floor), :656-672 (allow intersect + ensure_roots_narrow), :680-689 (project MCP can only disable or narrow to user-configured servers), :705-711 (floor re-enforced)
one_why: Clean positive counterexample to memcode clone-and-run (hook-trust-scoping x16 mostly holes): opening a hostile checkout cannot widen the agent's authority because every project-config merge is intersection-only; gemini-cli policy work's simpler sibling.

subject: ferrum
title: ~19k LOC of property tests + 21-task bench harness with zero workflow files - nothing ever executes them
evidence: find . -name '*.yml' -o -name '*.yaml' = 0 files repo-wide; tests/acp_stdio.rs:1; bench/README.md:3; src/tools/shell_guard.rs:695-940 (tier matrices that never run)
one_why: Instance x11 of test-suite-without-ci; ferrum's sharpest variant: the security policy's entire regression record is unenforced, and even the manual doc-drift gate (scripts/check-release-docs.sh) has no runner - single-maintainer good engineering with zero mechanical guarantee.

subject: ferrum
title: 'Ferrum is not a sandbox' - containment.md self-labeled design note, low tier honestly called not-a-hostile-input-boundary
one_why: Instance x10 of security-posture-docs and near-ceiling honesty: the doc names what the controls do NOT cover (allowed-executable behavior, $HOME, network) and credits an external security review by name; pairs with prime-agent removed-docs as the polarity reference.

subject: ferrum
title: Published security.md tier-by-command matrix is pinned by test (tier_capability_contract_is_table_driven)
one_why: No corpus prior (architecture-contract-test is a different axis): the doc's capability table and the guard's behavior cannot drift apart because the test drives off the same table - security docs that stay true by construction.

subject: ferrum
title: agent/mod.rs 10,178 LOC (~7,076 non-test) fuses loop, TUI completion/pickers, slash commands, compaction, and system prompt
one_why: File-scale sibling of grok-build's candidate monolithic-turn-function; AgentEventSink (src/agent/events.rs) decouples UI from loop but the split was never made physical - the pi-errata >5k-LOC product-file docking case, and why a cleanly-moduled tree still lands architecture 6.

subject: ferrum
title: Pre-request projection = max(provider-usage + new-message estimate, local estimate); still-over-budget after compaction hard-BLOCKS the send
evidence: src/agent/mod.rs:1782-1796 (projected_request_tokens), :4345,4376-4383 (phase checks + bail), :62 (95% threshold), src/agent/messages.rs:11 (untrusted summary prefix)
one_why: Second clean occupant of the gemini-cli-consolidated id: usage-feedback-aware trigger with staleness guarded by max(), plus a rare fail-closed send path - compaction failure refuses the request instead of overflowing the window; the fail-closed-bail is the hotdog-fit piece.

subject: ferrum
title: ACP editor mode defaults to --permissions Off: hosts get grammar policy only, zero client prompts
evidence: src/cli.rs:82 (default_value_t = AcpPermissionPolicy::Off), src/acp.rs:1539 (handler installed only when Ask)
one_why: Editor users (Zed per docs/zed.md) plausibly expect ACP requestPermission semantics by default; ferrum's grammar gate still binds, so bounded - but 'the protocol has a permission method' and 'we call it by default' are different shipped postures (forge undocumented-safe-off family, mildest rung, here documented in --help).
